meta.subtitle: From a 1995 Silicon Valley networking-chip startup to a $5B+ AI custom-silicon backlog with Amazon and Microsoft — how Sutardja's company became Matt Murphy's hyperscaler ASIC partner
meta.abstract: Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL, NASDAQ) is the Santa Clara-headquartered fabless semiconductor company that has, in the eight years since Matt Murphy became CEO in July 2016, transformed from a networking-and-storage chip vendor into one of the two structurally-important US merchant suppliers of AI-data-centre custom silicon — alongside Broadcom. The company traces its origins to the 1995 founding by Dr. Sehat Sutardja, his wife Weili Dai, and brother Pantas Sutardja as a fabless networking-chip startup. Through the 2000s and 2010s Marvell scaled across storage controllers (the disk-drive read-channel business that anchored early revenue), Ethernet networking silicon, and broader connectivity products. The strategic re-orientation under Murphy was deliberate: the 2018 $6 billion acquisition of Cavium added the ThunderX Arm server processor and the LiquidIO networking accelerator portfolios; the 2019 acquisition of Avera Semiconductor (the former IBM custom-silicon ASIC group) added custom-ASIC design capability at advanced process nodes; the 2020 $10 billion acquisition of Inphi added the PAM-DSP coherent-optics IP and the hyperscaler-data-centre optical interconnect customer relationships; the 2022 $1.1 billion acquisition of Innovium added the Teralynx switch-silicon line that competes directly with Broadcom Tomahawk. The current product franchise sits across five reporting segments: Data Center (the dominant growth driver, anchored by custom-ASIC programmes for hyperscalers and the PAM-DSP / Teralynx / electro-optics portfolios), Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer, and Automotive/Industrial. Fiscal year 2026 (ended early February 2026) produced annual revenue of approximately $7.0-7.5 billion with Data Center contributing well over half of the mix at materially higher gross margins than the legacy segments. The custom-ASIC backlog with Amazon (Trainium custom silicon), Microsoft (Maia 2 generation custom silicon), Google (TPU adjacent collaboration), and emerging hyperscaler programmes has been publicly characterised by management as multi-billion-dollar over the multi-year contracted horizon. CEO Matt Murphy continues to lead the company through this strategic transformation alongside an executive bench including President and COO Chris Koopmans, CFO Willem Meintjes (joined September 2024 from Pure Storage), and the deep technology leadership inherited from the Cavium, Inphi, and Innovium acquisitions. The investment proposition compresses AI custom-silicon design-win sustainability, the structural duopoly with Broadcom at the hyperscaler ASIC layer, the optical-interconnect cycle continuation, and the legacy-segment headwinds in Enterprise Networking and Carrier.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## The Structural Shift

Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL, Nasdaq) entered fiscal 2024 with its Data Center end market at $2.217 billion, or 40% of revenue, under the company's then-five-end-market disclosure. By fiscal 2025 that figure had risen to $4.164 billion, or 72% of revenue, and by fiscal 2026 it had reached $6.100 billion, or 74% of a record $8.195 billion [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The migration was not incremental. It was the formal restatement, in Marvell's own filings, of a company whose economic centre of gravity had moved to custom silicon, optical interconnect and cloud infrastructure.

The reporting architecture changed with the business. Marvell's fiscal 2025 annual report still broke revenue into five end markets: Data Center, Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer, and Automotive/Industrial [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). Beginning in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, however, the company consolidated Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer and Automotive/Industrial into a single "Communications and Other" line, while leaving Data Center unchanged [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). That accounting change did not create the mix shift; it acknowledged how dominant Data Center had already become.

Matt Murphy had served as chief executive since July 2016 and, by May 2026, also served as board chair, a role Marvell said became effective at the June 2023 annual meeting [Marvell board changes](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-announces-changes-board-of-directors-2023.html). Chris Koopmans served as President and Chief Operating Officer. Willem Meintjes, who joined in 2016, became chief financial officer effective January 20, 2023 after serving as chief accounting officer and treasurer since 2018 [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition) [Marvell executive team](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership.html).

## The Acquisition Arc

The Data Center franchise visible in fiscal 2026 was largely assembled through four Murphy-era deals. Cavium closed on July 6, 2018 and brought server, security and networking silicon into the portfolio [Cavium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-18-213486/d860055dex991.htm). Avera Semiconductor, the ASIC business of GlobalFoundries, closed on November 5, 2019 with net deal consideration of approximately $600 million after working-capital adjustments; Marvell described it as an infrastructure-ASIC platform with deep IBM heritage, roughly 800 technologists and more than 2,000 historical designs [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi) [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). Inphi closed on April 20, 2021, redomiciling the combined group into a Delaware parent and giving Marvell an electro-optics franchise with Ford Tamer joining the board at close [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi). Innovium closed on October 5, 2021, not 2022, adding cloud-optimised Ethernet switching and the Teralynx line [Innovium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/262/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-innovium).

## Revenue Architecture, FY2023-FY2026

| Fiscal year | Total revenue (USD) | Data Center revenue | Data Center share |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | $5.920 billion | $2.409 billion | 41% |
| FY2024 | $5.508 billion | $2.217 billion | 40% |
| FY2025 | $5.767 billion | $4.164 billion | 72% |
| FY2026 | $8.195 billion | $6.100 billion | 74% |

*Sources: [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) and [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).*

The fiscal 2026 surge was genuine rather than a classification artefact. Revenue rose 42% from $5.767 billion to $8.195 billion, while Data Center alone grew from $4.164 billion to $6.100 billion [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The first quarter of fiscal 2026, reported on May 29, 2025, produced $1.895 billion of revenue, of which Data Center contributed $1.441 billion, or 76% of the total [Marvell Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/95/marvell-technology-inc-reports-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results). That filing was a fiscal 2026 quarter and sat inside the period under review.

## Custom Silicon: From Zero to Roughly $1.5 Billion

The company no longer needed third-party arithmetic to establish the scale of the custom-silicon franchise. Marvell's 2026 proxy said custom silicon had grown from effectively zero to approximately 25% of Data Center revenue in fiscal 2026 [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm). Applied to the fiscal 2026 Data Center base of $6.100 billion, that implied roughly $1.5 billion of custom-silicon revenue - the figure cited repeatedly by management and consistent with the proxy's description of the business mix [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm) [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm).

The more important factual update was breadth. In May 2025 Marvell said it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers on custom XPUs and CPUs, custom network-interface controllers, CXL controllers and other accelerated-infrastructure devices [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). In August 2025 Murphy said Marvell was engaged in more than 50 new custom-AI opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf). In March 2026 he added that fiscal 2026 design wins had reached an all-time record and that bookings were continuing to grow at a record pace [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). Those disclosures established breadth more firmly than transcript-era design-win shorthand.

## The Optical Interconnect Franchise

The Inphi acquisition's most durable strategic contribution remained optics. Marvell's March 2026 release on its 1.6T DSP portfolio said the company had first introduced a 200G-per-lane 1.6T DSP in 5nm with Nova in 2023, followed it with the 3nm Ara platform in 2024, and by March 2026 was shipping Ara in mass volume to global customers [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity). A companion March 2026 release said Marvell had also introduced the industry's first 1.6T ZR/ZR+ pluggable and 2nm coherent DSPs, with sampling expected in the second half of 2026 [Marvell coherent-DSP release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1010/marvell-extends-zrzr-leadership-with-industry-first-1-6t-zrzr-pluggable-and-2nm-coherent-dsps-for-secure-ai-scale-across-interconnects).

Those releases mattered because they grounded the 1.6T story in product cadence rather than transcript rhetoric. By May 2026, Marvell had primary-source evidence for 5nm, 3nm and 2nm optics milestones and for mass-volume shipments of its current-generation 1.6T PAM4 platform.

## The Central Tension

The central question was no longer whether Marvell had reached hyperscaler scale. Its own filings answered that. The harder question was durability. Murphy said in the March 2026 fiscal-year release that Marvell expected year-over-year revenue growth to accelerate each quarter in fiscal 2027, driven by continued strength in Data Center, and that bookings were growing at a record pace [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). The first-quarter fiscal 2027 guide, issued before the frozen date, called for roughly $2.4 billion of revenue [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm).

What remained to be proved was whether the mix could keep compounding once the first custom-silicon ramps annualised, whether optical leadership at 1.6T converted cleanly from qualification to broad deployment, and whether Marvell's widening hyperscaler footprint translated into revenue concentration that was manageable rather than destabilising. The chapters that followed addressed those three questions from the filings outward, not from transcript extrapolation back.

---

**Primary sources used in this chapter:** [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) · [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm) · [Marvell Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/95/marvell-technology-inc-reports-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results) · [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf) · [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm) · [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm) · [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html) · [Marvell board changes](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-announces-changes-board-of-directors-2023.html) · [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition).

chapters.title: From the Sutardja era through the 2016 Murphy succession to the AI custom silicon inflection
chapters.body:
## The Sutardja Era: 1995-2016

Marvell's operating lineage began in 1995 under Sehat Sutardja, Weili Dai and Pantas Sutardja. The predecessor company, Marvell Technology Group Ltd., expanded from storage-control silicon into a broader networking-and-connectivity portfolio and reached public markets in June 2000 under the MRVL ticker. By the early 2010s the franchise had become meaningful in storage controllers, Ethernet and embedded processing, but it remained tied to businesses whose growth profile was increasingly cyclical or structurally mature.

One corporate-cleanup point mattered for the legal history: the business founded in 1995 and the Delaware corporation that existed at the end of the period under review were not technically the same parent. When Marvell completed the Inphi transaction on April 20, 2021, Marvell and Inphi became wholly owned subsidiaries of the new Delaware parent, Marvell Technology, Inc. [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi). That redomiciling step meant the business founded in 1995 and the Delaware parent at the end of the period under review were not technically the same corporate parent.

## Murphy and the Strategic Reset

Matt Murphy arrived in July 2016 from Maxim Integrated. The strategic change under him was not primarily rhetorical. It consisted of portfolio pruning, a willingness to exit businesses that no longer fit the target architecture, and a sustained effort to accumulate infrastructure IP rather than chase consumer or handset cycles. The later sale of the automotive Ethernet business to Infineon for $2.5 billion showed that this discipline continued well into the AI cycle: Marvell explicitly said the divestiture reflected its transformation into a data-infrastructure company, with Data Center already driving 75% of fourth-quarter fiscal 2025 revenue [Marvell automotive-sale announcement](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/101/marvell-to-sell-automotive-ethernet-business-to-infineon-for-2-5-billion-in-cash).

## The Acquisition Arc: 2018-2021, Not 2018-2022

The acquisition chronology ran as follows. Cavium closed on July 6, 2018 [Cavium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-18-213486/d860055dex991.htm). Avera closed on November 5, 2019, not September 2019, with Marvell describing the business as an ASIC provider backed by roughly 800 technologists, more than 2,000 historical designs and a material inherited revenue base [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi). Inphi closed on April 20, 2021 [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi). Innovium closed on October 5, 2021, not October 2022 [Innovium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/262/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-innovium).

Those dates were more than housekeeping. They changed how one read the AI inflection. By the time generative-AI infrastructure spending accelerated, Marvell already owned Avera's ASIC capability, Inphi's optical franchise and Innovium's cloud-switching assets. The portfolio was in place before the revenue wave became obvious in the income statement.

## The AI Custom-Silicon Inflection

The company filings made the mix shift unambiguous. Under Marvell's fiscal 2025 five-end-market presentation, Data Center accounted for 41% of revenue in fiscal 2023, 40% in fiscal 2024 and then jumped to 72% in fiscal 2025 [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). In the next annual report, after Marvell consolidated the non-Data-Center categories into Communications and Other, Data Center stood at 74% of fiscal 2026 revenue [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).

The accompanying customer and product disclosures sharpened the picture. In December 2024 Marvell announced a five-year, multi-generational AWS agreement covering custom AI products, optical DSPs, active electrical cable DSPs, PCIe retimers, DCI optical modules and Ethernet switching silicon [Marvell-AWS 8-K release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-24-000193/final2024_12x02xmarvell-.htm). In May 2025 Marvell said it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers on custom XPUs and CPUs as well as custom NICs, CXL controllers and other devices [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). In August 2025 Murphy said the team was engaged in more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf). Those disclosures established the public-record basis for describing Marvell as a hyperscaler ASIC franchise.

## Executive Evolution: the Meintjes Succession, January 2023

Marvell announced on January 11, 2023 that Willem Meintjes, who had joined in 2016 and had served as chief accounting officer and treasurer since 2018, would become chief financial officer effective January 20, 2023 following Jean Hu's resignation [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition). By 23 May 2026 he had therefore been in the role for more than three years, including through the period in which Data Center moved from a majority business to a roughly three-quarters business.

A parallel governance change also mattered. Marvell said on May 3, 2023 that Murphy would become chair of the board effective at the June 16, 2023 annual meeting, succeeding Rick Hill [Marvell board changes](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-announces-changes-board-of-directors-2023.html). By May 2026, Marvell's own disclosures showed Murphy as chair.

Taken together, the record showed an internally continuous transformation: Murphy took the chief executive role in 2016, Meintjes moved into the CFO seat in early 2023, Murphy assumed the chair in mid-2023, and the AI mix shift then surfaced in the fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 disclosures with unusual speed.

chapters.title: Data Center, Carrier Infrastructure, Enterprise Networking, Auto/Industrial
chapters.body:
## A Franchise Redrawn Around the Hyperscaler

The segment map Marvell used by May 2026 had changed materially by fiscal 2026. Marvell did not continue to report five standing end markets in the form used in earlier years. The fiscal 2025 annual report still presented five categories - Data Center, Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer, and Automotive/Industrial [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). Beginning in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, however, Marvell said it had consolidated Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer and Automotive/Industrial into a new "Communications and Other" end market, while leaving Data Center unchanged [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).

That change sharpened rather than softened the story. Under the older five-end-market presentation, Data Center had already reached 72% of revenue in fiscal 2025. Under the newer presentation it was 74% in fiscal 2026 [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).

## Data Center: Four Pillars Around One Spending Cycle

Marvell's own product disclosures showed that the Data Center end market bundled more than one business. The fiscal 2025 10-K described data-center applications to include cloud and on-premise AI systems, Ethernet switching, AI servers, general-purpose servers, DCI and storage systems [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). In practice the end market rested on four major product pillars.

**Custom silicon** became the strategic crown. Avera brought the ASIC platform, while later releases showed that Marvell had extended that platform into advanced packaging, custom HBM, CXL controllers, custom NICs and XPU-attach silicon [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi) [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). The December 2024 AWS agreement explicitly covered custom AI products, and by May 2025 Marvell said it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers [Marvell-AWS 8-K release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-24-000193/final2024_12x02xmarvell-.htm) [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html).

**Electro-optics** was the second pillar. Marvell's March 2026 1.6T release said the company had introduced Nova in 2023, Ara in 2024 and, by May 2026, was shipping Ara in mass volume [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity). The optical franchise was therefore not an abstract adjacency to AI; it was a shipping bandwidth product family inside the same Data Center line.

**Ethernet switching** entered through Innovium but had advanced materially by May 2026. Marvell said in July 2024 that Teralynx 10, its 51.2 Tbps switch, was in volume production with customer deployments under way [Marvell Teralynx 10 release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-teralynx-512t-ethernet-switch-enters-volume-production-for-global-ai-cloud-deployments.html). That mattered because the switch line gave Marvell something more credible than a design-service story: it could sell the surrounding network fabric as well as custom compute silicon.

**Storage controllers** remained the oldest pillar. The 10-K continued to describe HDD and SSD controllers, Fibre Channel and storage accelerators as part of Marvell's portfolio [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). They no longer drove the multiple, but they remained part of the company's cash-generation base.

## The Historical Non-Data-Center Buckets

The older reporting buckets still mattered because they described what had been subordinated.

**Enterprise Networking** covered campus and small-business routers, switches, wireless access points and network appliances [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm).

**Carrier Infrastructure** covered broadband-access systems, optical transport, routers and wireless RAN systems [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm).

**Consumer** covered broadband gateways, gaming consoles, PCs, printers, set-top boxes and home data storage [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm).

**Automotive/Industrial** covered ADAS, autonomous-vehicle, in-vehicle networking, industrial Ethernet and government products [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). One important update did not survive into later drafts: Marvell agreed in April 2025 to sell the Automotive Ethernet business to Infineon for $2.5 billion and completed that sale on August 14, 2025; after August 15, 2025 Marvell said the financials would no longer include contributions from that business [Marvell automotive-sale announcement](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/101/marvell-to-sell-automotive-ethernet-business-to-infineon-for-2-5-billion-in-cash) [Marvell automotive-sale closing](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/88/marvell-completes-divestiture-of-automotive-ethernet-business-to-infineon-for-2-5-billion-in-all-cash-transaction).

## The Mix Shift in Numbers

| End market | FY2023 share | FY2024 share | FY2025 share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data Center | 41% | 40% | 72% |
| Enterprise Networking | 23% | 22% | 11% |
| Carrier Infrastructure | 18% | 19% | 6% |
| Consumer | 12% | 11% | 5% |
| Automotive/Industrial | 6% | 8% | 6% |

*Source: [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm).*

For fiscal 2026 the company reported only two categories: Data Center at 74% and Communications and Other at 26% [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The point was not merely that Data Center had become the largest end market. It had become large enough that the old residual buckets were no longer the correct analytical frame.

chapters.title: $5.77B FY2025 revenue, Data Center segment majority, and the AI custom silicon scaling
chapters.body:
## A Revenue Trough, Then an Officially Disclosed Re-Rating

Marvell's published numbers showed a sharp internal transformation. Revenue moved from $5.920 billion in fiscal 2023 to $5.508 billion in fiscal 2024, recovered modestly to $5.767 billion in fiscal 2025, and then accelerated to a record $8.195 billion in fiscal 2026 [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The crucial line was not total revenue but end-market composition: Data Center was 41% of revenue in fiscal 2023, 40% in fiscal 2024, 72% in fiscal 2025 and 74% in fiscal 2026 [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).

## Revenue Trajectory and Mix

| Fiscal year | Period end | Total revenue | Data Center revenue | Data Center share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | Jan. 28, 2023 | $5.920B | $2.409B | 41% |
| FY2024 | Feb. 3, 2024 | $5.508B | $2.217B | 40% |
| FY2025 | Feb. 1, 2025 | $5.767B | $4.164B | 72% |
| FY2026 | Jan. 31, 2026 | $8.195B | $6.100B | 74% |

*Sources: [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) and [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).*

That progression altered the interpretation of the fiscal 2024-25 period. What had looked like a company trapped in a cyclical slump was, in hindsight, a company whose legacy buckets were shrinking while a new Data Center core was compounding rapidly enough to take the mix from roughly two-fifths to nearly three-quarters in two years.

## Data Center's Economic Weight

The 2026 proxy added a second useful data point: Marvell said custom silicon had reached approximately 25% of Data Center revenue in fiscal 2026, while optical interconnect represented roughly half [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm). On the fiscal 2026 Data Center base of $6.100 billion, that implied custom silicon of about $1.5 billion and optics of roughly $3.0 billion. The remaining quarter sat in switching, storage and adjacent products. That arithmetic made clear why investors began treating Marvell less as a legacy semis basket and more as an AI-infrastructure platform.

## Profit, Cash Flow and One Important Distortion

There was also a necessary correction to the way fiscal 2026 earnings were read. The March 2026 fourth-quarter release said Marvell generated $2.670 billion of GAAP net income and $2.466 billion of non-GAAP net income in fiscal 2026, with $1.751 billion of cash flow from operations [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). But the same filing showed a $1.830 billion gain on sale of business in the cash-flow reconciliation, reflecting the Automotive Ethernet divestiture [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). In other words, GAAP earnings in fiscal 2026 captured both the operating surge and a large divestiture gain. For operating analysis, the end-market mix, non-GAAP earnings and Data Center disclosures were the cleaner measures.

## R&D Intensity and the Real Capital Load

Custom silicon was R&D-intensive, and the filings provided firmer numbers. Marvell spent $1.950 billion on research and development in fiscal 2025 and $2.075 billion in fiscal 2026 [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). In fiscal 2025 that was roughly 34% of revenue; in fiscal 2026 it fell to about 25% as revenue expanded faster than expense. That decline did not mean the technical load had eased. It meant the AI ramps had finally begun absorbing the fixed cost base.

The same pattern appeared in capex and working capital. Marvell remained fabless, so property and equipment at January 31, 2026 stood at $935 million rather than anything like an integrated-manufacturer asset base [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). But inventories had risen to $1.388 billion and accounts receivable to $2.187 billion as the company scaled shipments into a more concentrated, high-volume cloud base [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). In custom silicon, economic investment ran through design resources, package engineering, prepayments for supply and inventory build, not just through classical plant capex.

## Balance Sheet and Capital Allocation

By January 31, 2026 Marvell reported $2.639 billion of cash and cash equivalents against $3.971 billion of long-term debt and $500 million of short-term debt [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). The balance sheet still carried the legacy of the acquisition era, but the auto-Ethernet sale and rising Data Center cash flows had increased flexibility. In the March 2025 fiscal-year release, Murphy said Marvell had returned $933 million to stockholders in fiscal 2025 through buybacks and dividends [Marvell Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/109/marvell-technology-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results). By fiscal 2026 the balance-sheet question was less whether Marvell could service the acquisition-era capital structure and more whether it could keep funding custom programs, optics and switching at the pace hyperscaler demand now required.

## The Genuine Inflection

Fiscal 2026 was a 74% Data Center year, not a 70% one. More important, the retrospective numbers showed that the real jump had already occurred a year earlier, when Data Center moved from 40% to 72% of revenue between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025 [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). Fiscal 2026 was not the birth of the new Marvell. It was the year the new Marvell became impossible to miss.

chapters.title: From the 2016 Murphy era to the 2024 AI custom silicon inflection
chapters.body:
## The Succession Brief and the Transformation Mandate

When Murphy arrived in July 2016, Marvell still looked like a diversified infrastructure-chip company with meaningful storage, enterprise and carrier exposure. By May 2026 the official record described something very different: a business in which Data Center accounted for 74% of fiscal 2026 revenue and custom silicon, optics and switching formed the core of the growth narrative [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm).

## The Acquisition Arc as Earnings Thesis

The earnings story became legible only after the acquisition timeline was corrected. Cavium closed in July 2018, Avera in November 2019, Inphi in April 2021 and Innovium in October 2021 [Cavium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-18-213486/d860055dex991.htm) [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi) [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi) [Innovium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/262/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-innovium). By the time Marvell began disclosing a hyperscaler-custom-silicon story in earnest, the technical stack had already been assembled.

## The Inventory Correction, Then the Mix Shock

Fiscal 2024 still read like a correction year. Revenue fell to $5.508 billion from $5.920 billion, and the legacy end markets remained material [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). But the same 10-K showed that Data Center already represented 40% of revenue in fiscal 2024 and then jumped to 72% in fiscal 2025, even though total company revenue rose only modestly to $5.767 billion [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). That was the real earnings inflection: the headline recovery understated the internal re-rating.

## What Management Actually Said During the Ramp

The primary releases provided a cleaner chronology than the third-party transcript stack.

On March 5, 2025, Marvell reported fourth-quarter and fiscal-year 2025 results. Murphy said the custom AI silicon programs had entered volume production and that Marvell expected first-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue growth of more than 60% year on year at the midpoint of guidance [Marvell Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/109/marvell-technology-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results).

On May 29, 2025, Marvell reported first-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $1.895 billion, with Data Center at $1.441 billion, or 76% of total revenue [Marvell Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/95/marvell-technology-inc-reports-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results). That quarter mattered because it showed the AI story had moved from guidance into printed revenue.

On August 28, 2025, Marvell reported second-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue of $2.006 billion. Murphy said the company's custom-AI design activity was at an all-time high and that the team was engaged in more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf).

On March 5, 2026, Marvell reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $8.195 billion and said fiscal 2026 design wins had hit an all-time record. Murphy added that year-over-year revenue growth was expected to accelerate each quarter in fiscal 2027 and that bookings were continuing to grow at a record pace [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm).

## The CFO Question Had Already Been Resolved

Marvell's own filing placed the CFO transition in January 2023, when Meintjes succeeded Jean Hu effective January 20, 2023 [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition). By the time Data Center crossed the 70% threshold, Meintjes had already been CFO throughout the crucial build-and-ramp period.

## What the Earnings Arc Ultimately Showed

The eight years from Murphy's arrival to fiscal 2026 did not tell the story of a cyclical rebound. They told the story of a company whose earnings structure was remade underneath a still-semiconductor-looking revenue line, and then surfaced all at once. The filings showed the sequence cleanly: custom programs entered volume production in early calendar 2025, Data Center ran at 76% of revenue in the May 2025 quarter, design activity broadened into more than 50 opportunities by August 2025, and fiscal 2026 closed with record design wins and a record revenue base by March 2026 [Marvell Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/109/marvell-technology-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results) [Marvell Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/95/marvell-technology-inc-reports-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results) [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf) [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm).

chapters.title: Murphy, Meintjes, Koopmans, segment GMs, and the post-Sutardja board
chapters.body:
## The Succession and the Transformation Mandate

By 23 May 2026 the broad shape of Marvell's leadership was straightforward to verify because the company published both an executive-team page and a current board page.

Matt Murphy remained chairman and chief executive officer [Marvell executive team](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership.html) [Marvell board of directors](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership/board-of-directors.html). Marvell had announced in May 2023 that Murphy would become chair effective at the June 16, 2023 annual meeting, succeeding Rick Hill [Marvell board changes](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-announces-changes-board-of-directors-2023.html). By May 2026, the company's own disclosures showed Murphy as chair.

## The Operational Backbone

Chris Koopmans served as President and Chief Operating Officer [Marvell executive team](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership.html). That preserved Cavium-era operational continuity. Murphy handled the external narrative; Koopmans remained central to scale, execution and portfolio integration.

The Data Center-heavy organisation was also more visible than before. Marvell's executive-team page listed Sandeep Bharathi as President of the Data Center Group, Will Chu as Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Custom Cloud Solutions Business, Dave Lazovsky as Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center Networking Business Group, Noam Mizrahi as corporate chief technology officer, and Xi Wang as Senior Vice President and General Manager of the Connectivity Group [Marvell executive team](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership.html). Those titles mattered because they showed how the company itself had chosen to describe the centre of managerial gravity: custom cloud solutions, data-center networking, connectivity and platform technology, not legacy enterprise or consumer franchises.

## The CFO Transition at the Inflection Point

Willem Meintjes was central to the finance succession story. Marvell announced on January 11, 2023 that he would become chief financial officer effective January 20, 2023, after having served as chief accounting officer and treasurer since 2018 [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition). The company said he had joined in 2016 as senior vice president of finance and had previously been vice president and corporate controller at Newport Corporation and International Rectifier [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition). He was therefore an internal finance successor rather than a late outside recruit.

That timing also changed the analytical read. Meintjes was not a late-cycle finance hire brought in after the AI thesis had already been won. He was an internal successor who bridged the legacy portfolio, the M&A integration years and the custom-silicon ramp itself.

## The Board as of May 2026

The board page as of 23 May 2026 listed Murphy plus eight other directors: Sara Andrews, Tudor Brown, Brad Buss, Daniel Durn, Rebecca House, Marachel Knight, Rajiv Ramaswami and Rick Wallace [Marvell board of directors](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership/board-of-directors.html). That current board composition showed how far the board had turned over from earlier phases of the company's history. Some former directors had served Marvell historically, but they were not the board shown by the company itself in May 2026.

The practical implication was that Marvell's board had rotated with the business. The current group blended semiconductor, enterprise-infrastructure and operating backgrounds, but the company no longer presented the board as an Inphi-transition or cybersecurity-governance story. It presented it as the board of an AI-infrastructure semiconductor company led by a combined chair and CEO.

## A Team Shaped by the Business It Became

The leadership architecture visible in the primary sources was therefore clear and internally consistent. Murphy was not merely the long-tenured strategist; he was also the sitting chair. Meintjes was not an external 2024 recruit; he was a 2016-era internal finance operator elevated in early 2023. And the operating bench by May 2026 was explicitly organised around data-center groups, custom cloud solutions, networking and connectivity [Marvell executive team](https://www.marvell.com/company/leadership.html). In assessing whether Marvell had truly become a hyperscaler ASIC franchise, that last point mattered as much as the titles themselves.

chapters.title: Hyperscalers, TSMC foundry, advanced packaging, and HBM supply
chapters.body:
By early 2026 the defining fact about Marvell's customer and supply-chain profile was concentration around cloud and AI infrastructure rather than broad diversification across end markets.

## The Custom-Silicon Franchise: What Was Publicly Confirmed

The cleanest primary-source evidence on the customer side came from Marvell itself. In December 2024 Marvell announced an expanded five-year, multi-generational agreement with AWS. The company said the agreement covered a broad range of data-center semiconductors, including custom AI products, optical DSPs, active electrical cable DSPs, PCIe retimers, DCI optical modules and Ethernet switching silicon [Marvell-AWS 8-K release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-24-000193/final2024_12x02xmarvell-.htm). That language documented the breadth of Marvell's commercial footprint inside AWS.

Microsoft's Maia program was also publicly real, though the primary source for the product itself came from Microsoft rather than Marvell. Microsoft unveiled Azure Maia on November 15, 2023 as its custom AI accelerator for training and inference workloads in the Microsoft Cloud [Microsoft official blog](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2023/11/15/microsoft-ignite-2023-ai-transformation-and-the-technology-driving-change//) [Microsoft Source feature](https://news.microsoft.com/source/features/ai/in-house-chips-silicon-to-service-to-meet-ai-demand/?msockid=215a59bf8fe26ca811064ff88e346d71). Marvell did not, in its primary filings before 23 May 2026, publish a product-specific revenue bridge for Maia. What it did say, in May 2025, was that it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers on custom XPUs and CPUs, custom NICs, CXL controllers and other devices for clouds and AI clusters [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html).

Meta appeared in the primary record through networking rather than an unnamed "data-processing-unit engagement." At OCP in October 2024 Marvell said it had partnered with Meta to develop FBNIC, a custom 5nm Ethernet NIC designed for Meta's infrastructure [Marvell FBNIC release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/124/marvell-delivers-custom-ethernet-network-interface-controller-solution-at-open-compute-project). That was narrower, but also more defensible because it came from a named company release.

## Breadth of Design Activity

Marvell's own later earnings releases reinforced that these were not isolated sockets. In August 2025 Murphy said custom-AI design activity was at an all-time high, with more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf). In March 2026 he added that fiscal 2026 design wins had reached an all-time record and that bookings were continuing to grow at a record pace [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). That was the best primary-source answer to the question of whether the customer roster had broadened beyond a few flagship relationships.

## Electro-Optics at Scale

The optics side of the franchise was just as important to the customer map. Marvell said in March 2026 that Ara, its 3nm 1.6T PAM4 platform introduced in December 2024, was already shipping in mass volume to global customers and enabling hyperscalers and cloud providers to deploy 1.6T pluggable connectivity [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity) [Marvell Ara release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/120/marvell-unveils-industrys-first-3nm-1-6-tbps-pam4-interconnect-platform-to-scale-accelerated-infrastructure). A second March 2026 release added that Marvell's new 2nm coherent DSPs and 1.6T ZR/ZR+ pluggables were expected to begin sampling in the second half of 2026 [Marvell coherent-DSP release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1010/marvell-extends-zrzr-leadership-with-industry-first-1-6t-zrzr-pluggable-and-2nm-coherent-dsps-for-secure-ai-scale-across-interconnects). The product cadence therefore supported the commercial claim that Marvell was more than a custom-ASIC house.

## TSMC: the Foundry Backbone

On the supply side, Marvell's dependence on TSMC was explicit. The fiscal 2025 10-K said Marvell had successfully executed multiple 5nm designs, was progressing through 3nm designs, and was developing its advanced 2nm generation platform [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). In March 2024 Marvell and TSMC publicly described a collaboration on an industry-first 2nm platform for accelerated-infrastructure silicon, with Marvell saying the platform would underpin custom compute accelerators, Ethernet switches, optical and copper interconnect DSPs and other cloud-data-center devices [Marvell 2nm platform release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/153/marvell-announces-industrys-first-2nm-platform-for-accelerated-infrastructure-silicon).

The manufacturing dependency became even more concrete in Marvell's packaging disclosures. The May 2025 advanced-packaging release described a production-qualified multi-die platform that could integrate 1,390 square millimetres of silicon, four HBM3 or HBM3E stacks and six redistribution layers, and said the platform was qualified with a major hyperscaler and entering production ramp [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). Marvell's March 2024 2nm announcement and its later packaging release therefore framed TSMC not merely as a wafer supplier, but as the core process-and-packaging partner for the most strategic part of the business.

## HBM and Memory

Marvell's own disclosures on HBM were narrower than the broader market commentary around the category, but they were still informative. In December 2024 the company announced a custom HBM compute architecture that it said could deliver up to 25% more compute and 33% greater memory while improving power efficiency [Marvell custom HBM release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/117/marvell-announces-breakthrough-custom-hbm-compute-architecture-to-optimize-cloud-ai-accelerators). The same release said Marvell was working through strategic collaboration with leading memory makers. The May 2025 packaging release added support for HBM3 and HBM3E and said Marvell was actively qualifying the platform for future HBM4 designs [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). Those were the verifiable HBM facts inside the period under review.

## Geography and Export Controls

Marvell's official geography table complicated any simplistic low-China-exposure narrative. For fiscal 2026, shipments by destination went 36% to China, 20% to Taiwan, 14% to the United States and 30% to other markets [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). But the same filing warned that those destinations were not necessarily indicative of end-customer geography and said a substantial majority of shipments to China were for non-China-based customers with manufacturing there [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The right conclusion was therefore not that China had become irrelevant. It was that Marvell's reported shipment geography overstated its direct end-demand reliance on China, even as trade restrictions remained a disclosed risk.

The overall picture was of a company deeply tied to a small number of sophisticated cloud customers, heavily dependent on TSMC's process and packaging roadmap, and increasingly organised around AI-era bandwidth and memory constraints rather than around the old storage-controller franchise.

chapters.title: Where Marvell sits against Broadcom, Nvidia, AMD, and emerging custom silicon
chapters.body:
## The Custom-Silicon Argument, Restated on Primary Sources

Third-party reconstruction of Google, Broadcom and OpenAI relationships went beyond what Marvell itself disclosed. Marvell's own disclosures nonetheless supported a narrower but still strong competitive framing.

By May 2025 Marvell said it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers on custom XPUs and CPUs, custom NICs, CXL controllers and other accelerated-infrastructure devices [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). By August 2025 Murphy said the company was pursuing more than 50 new custom-AI opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf). By March 2026 he said fiscal 2026 design wins had reached an all-time record [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). That was enough to establish that Marvell had become one of the small number of merchant partners trusted inside the hyperscaler custom-compute stack, even without repeating customer maps that Marvell itself had not formally published.

## Where Marvell Actually Differentiated Itself

Marvell's competitive case rested on combination rather than on any single product.

First, there was the **custom-silicon platform**. Avera gave Marvell the full-ASIC base; later releases showed the company layering in advanced packaging, custom HBM, CXL, co-packaged copper, silicon photonics, NICs and XPU-attach technologies [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi) [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html) [Marvell custom HBM release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/117/marvell-announces-breakthrough-custom-hbm-compute-architecture-to-optimize-cloud-ai-accelerators).

Second, there was **optical interconnect**. Marvell's March 2026 1.6T release said Ara was already shipping in mass volume to global customers, while the company also positioned itself for the next coherent-DSP cycle with 2nm products scheduled to sample in the second half of 2026 [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity) [Marvell coherent-DSP release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1010/marvell-extends-zrzr-leadership-with-industry-first-1-6t-zrzr-pluggable-and-2nm-coherent-dsps-for-secure-ai-scale-across-interconnects).

Third, there was **switching**. Teralynx 10 had entered volume production by July 2024 as a 51.2 Tbps device with low latency and customer deployments under way [Marvell Teralynx 10 release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-teralynx-512t-ethernet-switch-enters-volume-production-for-global-ai-cloud-deployments.html). That made Marvell's pitch more credible with hyperscalers that wanted open-Ethernet AI fabrics rather than a standalone compute chip vendor.

## The Numbers That Best Captured Positioning

The clearest quantitative proxy for Marvell's position came from Marvell itself. In the 2026 proxy the company said custom silicon had grown from effectively zero to approximately 25% of Data Center revenue, while optical interconnect represented roughly half [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm). Because Data Center revenue totaled $6.100 billion in fiscal 2026, that implied a custom-silicon business of roughly $1.5 billion and an optics business of around $3 billion [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). In other words, the company was not valued merely on a hope that custom silicon might arrive. It had already arrived inside a much broader accelerated-infrastructure stack.

## Marvell Versus the Merchant-GPU World

One point remained essential: Marvell was not trying to compete with Nvidia or AMD on merchant accelerators product for product. Its role was to help customers replace, complement or connect those products through custom compute, optics, switches, memory and interfaces. Marvell's own releases made that point repeatedly. The AWS agreement covered custom AI products and connectivity. The Meta FBNIC announcement showed Marvell inside customer-specific infrastructure blocks. The packaging release described custom XPUs, CPUs, NICs and CXL controllers as parts of a single accelerated-infrastructure design space [Marvell-AWS 8-K release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-24-000193/final2024_12x02xmarvell-.htm) [Marvell FBNIC release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/124/marvell-delivers-custom-ethernet-network-interface-controller-solution-at-open-compute-project) [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html).

## The Durability Question

The competitive question therefore was not whether Marvell had carved out real hyperscaler relevance. The primary materials made clear that it had. The question was whether that relevance would remain durable once first-generation ramps annualised and customers reconsidered make-versus-buy boundaries on later generations.

The bullish evidence inside the period under review was concrete: all four top hyperscalers, more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers, record fiscal 2026 design wins, mass-volume 1.6T optics, volume-production 51.2T switching, and a custom-silicon business that had already reached roughly one quarter of Data Center revenue [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html) [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf) [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm) [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm).

The bear case remained equally clear: hyperscaler relationships were deep but concentrated, the technical bar kept rising, and larger incumbents still contested every layer of the stack. But the company no longer needed speculative reconstruction to argue that it occupied a real strategic seat.

chapters.title: From 2018 Cavium through Inphi, AI custom silicon, and the September 2024 CFO transition
chapters.body:
## The Acquisition Arc as Catalyst Timeline

Marvell's catalyst timeline ran in clear sequence. Cavium closed in July 2018, Avera in November 2019, Inphi in April 2021 and Innovium in October 2021 [Cavium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001193125-18-213486/d860055dex991.htm) [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi) [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi) [Innovium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/262/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-innovium). Placed in sequence, Innovium looked earlier and more strategic than a 2022 closing date would have implied.

Each of those deals became visible to investors on a different timetable. Cavium expanded the compute-and-networking base. Avera gave Marvell the full-ASIC substrate. Inphi added the electro-optics franchise. Innovium extended the cloud-switch story. None of them, by itself, created the 2025-26 equity narrative. Together they produced the platform that later AI demand could re-rate.

## The Product-Cycle Catalysts

The most important catalysts inside the period under review were product and customer disclosures rather than generic AI enthusiasm.

In December 2024 Marvell expanded its strategic relationship with AWS through a five-year, multi-generational agreement spanning custom AI products, optical DSPs, AEC DSPs, PCIe retimers, DCI modules and Ethernet switching silicon [Marvell-AWS 8-K release](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-24-000193/final2024_12x02xmarvell-.htm).

Also in December 2024 Marvell introduced Ara, which it described as the industry's first 3nm 1.6T PAM4 interconnect platform, reducing optical-module power by over 20% versus the prior generation [Marvell Ara release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/120/marvell-unveils-industrys-first-3nm-1-6-tbps-pam4-interconnect-platform-to-scale-accelerated-infrastructure).

That same month the company announced a custom HBM compute architecture it said could deliver up to 25% more compute and 33% greater memory, a notable signal that Marvell wanted to own more of the XPU bill of materials than simple design services [Marvell custom HBM release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/117/marvell-announces-breakthrough-custom-hbm-compute-architecture-to-optimize-cloud-ai-accelerators).

In May 2025 Marvell disclosed that it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers on custom XPUs and CPUs, NICs, CXL controllers and other devices, while also describing a production-qualified advanced-packaging platform that was already ramping with a major hyperscaler [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html).

## The Earnings Releases as Catalysts

The financial releases then converted that product narrative into reported numbers.

March 2025: custom AI silicon programs entered volume production, and the company guided to more than 60% year-over-year growth in first-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue at the midpoint [Marvell Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/109/marvell-technology-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2025-financial-results).

May 2025: first-quarter fiscal 2026 revenue printed at $1.895 billion, with Data Center contributing 76% [Marvell Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/95/marvell-technology-inc-reports-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results).

August 2025: second-quarter revenue rose to $2.006 billion, and Murphy said the company was engaged in over 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers [Marvell Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000187/0001835632-25-000187.pdf).

March 2026: fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $8.195 billion, fiscal 2026 design wins hit an all-time record, and management said year-over-year revenue growth should accelerate each quarter in fiscal 2027 [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm).

## The Divestiture Catalyst

One important catalyst was subtraction rather than addition. Marvell announced in April 2025 that it would sell its Automotive Ethernet business to Infineon for $2.5 billion, saying the business was expected to generate $225 million to $250 million of fiscal 2026 revenue [Marvell automotive-sale announcement](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/101/marvell-to-sell-automotive-ethernet-business-to-infineon-for-2-5-billion-in-cash). The transaction closed on August 14, 2025, and Marvell said its financials would no longer include contributions from that business after August 15 [Marvell automotive-sale closing](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/88/marvell-completes-divestiture-of-automotive-ethernet-business-to-infineon-for-2-5-billion-in-all-cash-transaction). The sale simplified the portfolio and reinforced management's willingness to concentrate capital behind higher-growth AI infrastructure.

## The CFO Transition, Correctly Dated

Meintjes succeeded Jean Hu effective January 20, 2023 [Marvell CFO transition](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/196/marvell-announces-cfo-transition). By the time the AI catalyst stack became visible in 2025 and 2026, the finance-function succession had long since been completed.

The through-line across all these events was straightforward: the AI catalyst story was not one press release, one quarter or one rumored socket. It was the cumulative effect of a cleaned-up portfolio, a broadened hyperscaler customer set, and the progression from 5nm to 3nm to 2nm-plus-packaging in the parts of the stack Marvell actually controlled.

chapters.title: Custom ASIC IP, PAM-DSP optics, Ethernet switch silicon, and the 5nm/3nm/2nm roadmap
chapters.body:
## The IP Mosaic

Marvell's technology moat was best understood as an accumulation of validated infrastructure IP rather than as a single hero product. The sources inside the period under review supported three major IP deposits.

Avera contributed the ASIC design engine. Marvell said at close that Avera brought roughly 800 technologists, more than 2,000 historical designs, deep IBM heritage and an IP base spanning SerDes, embedded memory and advanced packaging [Avera closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/347/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-avera-semi).

Inphi contributed the optical and coherent-DSP franchise that Marvell later extended into Nova, Ara and the 2nm coherent roadmap [Inphi closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/282/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-inphi) [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity) [Marvell coherent-DSP release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1010/marvell-extends-zrzr-leadership-with-industry-first-1-6t-zrzr-pluggable-and-2nm-coherent-dsps-for-secure-ai-scale-across-interconnects).

Innovium contributed the cloud-switch architecture that became Teralynx 10 [Innovium closing release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/262/marvell-completes-acquisition-of-innovium) [Marvell Teralynx 10 release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-teralynx-512t-ethernet-switch-enters-volume-production-for-global-ai-cloud-deployments.html).

## Custom-ASIC Design Engine

Marvell's annual report described the custom-ASIC offering as a platform built from differentiated internal IP including ultra-high-speed SerDes, Arm compute, security, storage, silicon photonics and advanced packaging, including die-to-die interconnects, chiplets, co-packaged optics and custom HBM [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). That was a precise description of the blocks Marvell itself said it was contributing.

The later product releases broadened the picture. In October 2024 Marvell said it had developed Meta's custom FBNIC on its 5nm accelerated-infrastructure silicon platform [Marvell FBNIC release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/124/marvell-delivers-custom-ethernet-network-interface-controller-solution-at-open-compute-project). In May 2025 it said it was working with all four top hyperscalers not only on XPUs and CPUs but also on NICs, CXL controllers and other devices [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). The custom business was therefore broader than a small set of training accelerators.

## Optical and Interconnect IP

Marvell's optical roadmap was unusually well documented in company materials. The March 2026 1.6T release said Marvell had introduced its first 200G-per-lane 1.6T DSP in 5nm with Nova in 2023, followed it with the 3nm Ara platform in 2024, and by March 2026 was shipping Ara in mass volume [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity). The December 2024 Ara launch said the new 3nm platform cut optical-module power by more than 20% [Marvell Ara release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/120/marvell-unveils-industrys-first-3nm-1-6-tbps-pam4-interconnect-platform-to-scale-accelerated-infrastructure).

On the coherent side, Marvell's March 2026 release described the industry's first 1.6T ZR/ZR+ pluggable and 2nm coherent DSPs, with customer sampling expected in the second half of 2026 [Marvell coherent-DSP release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1010/marvell-extends-zrzr-leadership-with-industry-first-1-6t-zrzr-pluggable-and-2nm-coherent-dsps-for-secure-ai-scale-across-interconnects). The point was not merely that Marvell had a roadmap; it had a multi-generation optical DSP sequence tied to specific process nodes and shipping milestones.

## Switch Silicon

Marvell's current switching story was not centred on 12.8 Tbps parts alone. In July 2024 the company said Teralynx 10, its programmable 51.2 Tbps Ethernet switch, had entered volume production with customer deployments under way [Marvell Teralynx 10 release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-teralynx-512t-ethernet-switch-enters-volume-production-for-global-ai-cloud-deployments.html). Marvell also said Teralynx 10 offered industry-best radix at 512 and latency as low as 500 nanoseconds [Marvell Teralynx 10 release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-teralynx-512t-ethernet-switch-enters-volume-production-for-global-ai-cloud-deployments.html). That mattered because it turned switching from a defensive adjacency into an AI-fabric product with its own shipping proof points.

## Process Nodes: 5nm, 3nm and 2nm

Marvell's annual report said the company had successfully executed multiple 5nm designs, was progressing through 3nm designs, and was developing its advanced 2nm generation platform [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm). The March 2024 2nm announcement added that the platform covered high-speed long-reach SerDes above 200 Gbps, processor subsystems, encryption engines, SoC fabrics, chip-to-chip interconnects and high-bandwidth physical interfaces for compute, memory, networking and storage [Marvell 2nm platform release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/153/marvell-announces-industrys-first-2nm-platform-for-accelerated-infrastructure-silicon).

The packaging layer was equally material. The May 2025 advanced-packaging release described a platform capable of integrating 1,390 square millimetres of silicon with four HBM3 or HBM3E stacks, and said the platform was already qualified with a major hyperscaler [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html). That was the missing factual bridge between node leadership and real AI-cluster hardware.

## R&D Intensity

Marvell spent $1.950 billion on R&D in fiscal 2025 and $2.075 billion in fiscal 2026 [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). In fiscal 2025 that equated to roughly one-third of revenue. The number mattered because it quantified the cost of maintaining simultaneous leadership efforts in custom compute, optics, switching, packaging and memory. The IP stack was broad because the spending had been broad.

chapters.title: Custom silicon programme concentration, Broadcom competitive intensity, AI cycle, China exposure
chapters.body:
Marvell's transformation into an AI-infrastructure company brought precisely the set of risks one would expect from a business increasingly tied to a few very large customers, one foundry ecosystem and a narrow band of advanced-node technologies. The better version of the bear case had to be anchored in Marvell's own disclosures rather than in general semiconductor folklore.

## Customer Concentration Inside Data Center

The first risk was concentration. Marvell's fiscal 2026 10-K showed Data Center at 74% of total revenue [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The 2026 proxy added that custom silicon represented approximately 25% of Data Center revenue [Marvell 2026 proxy](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-060253/tm261486-1_def14a.htm). The math implied that a large share of group economics had become dependent on a custom-compute activity tied to a small number of hyperscaler programs.

Marvell acknowledged the concentration risk more directly in its March 2026 earnings materials, which warned of dependence on a few customers and of a significant portion of sales being concentrated in the Data Center end market [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). The bullish counterargument was that Marvell also said it was collaborating with all four top hyperscalers and that design wins had hit an all-time record [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html) [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). But breadth of opportunity did not erase concentration of realized revenue.

## Competitive Intensity

The second risk was competitive intensity in exactly the categories driving the re-rating: custom silicon, optical interconnect and AI fabrics. Marvell's own materials showed it had built a credible position in all three, but they also showed how much technical execution the model required. The company was racing on process nodes, advanced packaging, HBM integration, 1.6T optics, CXL and switching simultaneously [Marvell 2nm platform release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/153/marvell-announces-industrys-first-2nm-platform-for-accelerated-infrastructure-silicon) [Marvell advanced-packaging release](https://www.marvell.com/company/newsroom/marvell-delivers-advanced-packaging-platform-custom-ai-accelerators.html) [Marvell 1.6T PAM4 release](https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1013/marvell-ushers-in-the-1-6t-era-with-expanded-optical-dsp-platform-portfolio-redefining-ai-data-center-end-to-end-connectivity). A company competing on that many fronts could lose relevance through slippage in any one of them.

## AI-Cycle Moderation

The third risk was cyclical. Marvell's recent numbers had been driven by robust AI demand, in Murphy's own phrasing [Marvell Q4 FY2026 results](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000006/q426_8kx1312026ex-991.htm). If that demand paused, the company's revenue mix offered less insulation than a few years earlier. Under the older five-end-market presentation, Enterprise Networking, Carrier Infrastructure, Consumer and Automotive/Industrial once collectively represented 60% of revenue in fiscal 2024. By fiscal 2026 the non-Data-Center businesses had been consolidated into Communications and Other and represented only 26% [Marvell FY2025 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-25-000057/mrvl-20250201.htm) [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). In other words, there was less ballast left if hyperscaler AI capex ever slowed.

## China and Trade Controls

The fourth risk required a careful reading. Marvell's fiscal 2026 geography table showed 36% of shipments by destination going to China, 20% to Taiwan and 14% to the United States [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). Yet the same filing said a substantial majority of shipments to China were for non-China-based customers with factories or contract manufacturers located there [Marvell FY2026 10-K](https://investor.marvell.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001835632-26-000011/mrvl-20260131.htm). The right risk framing was therefore twofold: Marvell remained materially exposed to Asian manufacturing geography, and it remained exposed to trade restrictions imposed on Chinese customers, but shipment data alone overstated direct China end-demand concentration.

## Foundry and Packaging Dependence

The fifth risk was supplier dependence.
